stem: Which of the following best describes sodium cromoglycate used in asthma management?

options.text: A mast cell stabiliser used as prophylaxis in asthma
A short-acting beta2 agonist used for immediate bronchodilation
An inhaled corticosteroid used as first-line controller therapy
A leukotriene receptor antagonist used for acute symptom relief

explanation: Sodium cromoglycate (cromolyn) is a mast cell stabiliser that helps prevent asthma symptoms by inhibiting mediator release; it is not a reliever medication and is used as prophylaxis rather than for acute bronchospasm.
rationale: The original item was a fill-in-the-blank prompt and not SBA-compatible, so it has been rewritten into a single-best-answer question preserving the asthma medication concept.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Sodium cromoglycate is a mast cell stabiliser used for asthma prophylaxis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. Short-acting beta2 agonists are bronchodilators used for rapid symptom relief.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. Inhaled corticosteroids are controller drugs, but sodium cromoglycate is not a corticosteroid.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. Leukotriene receptor antagonists are a different preventive drug class and are not sodium cromoglycate.
